Architecture firm Herzog & de Meuron Roche Tower (German: Roche-Turm ), also known as Building 1 (German: Bau 1 ), is an office skyscraper in the Swiss city of Basel . [ 1 ] Designed by Herzog & de Meuron for the pharmaceutical company Hoffmann-La Roche , it stands 178 metres (584 ft) tall with 41 floors. [ 1 ] At the time of its opening, it was the tallest building in Switzerland, surpassing the Prime Tower (126 meters) in Zürich by 52 metres. [ 1 ] The building has a total floor space of 74,200 m 2 (799,000 sq ft) and cost CHF 550 million to construct. It houses around 2,000 employees. [ 1 ] In 2020, Roche Tower was overtaken in height by the adjacent 205-metre Building 2, also developed by Roche. [ 2 ] History [ edit ] Construction of Building 1 began in 2012, and it was officially inaugurated on 18 September 2015. Strict planning regulations in Swiss cities mean that there are few skyscrapers in the country. [ 1 ] Architecture and engineering [ edit ] The structure stands on 143 piles driven up to 24 metres (79 ft) into the ground, topped by a foundation slab intended to enhance stability in earthquakes . [ 2 ] Basel lies in one of Switzerland’s highest-risk earthquake zones along with the canton of Valais . [ 2 ] The tower was engineered to withstand a magnitude 6.9 earthquake on the Richter scale , a standard higher than legally required, corresponding to an event statistically expected once every 1,500 years. [ 2 ] The building features a closed-cavity facade that reduces cleaning requirements, provides solar shading, and maintains outward visibility.
